```{r}
adata <- read_h5ad(file.path(dir_xen,"Graham_Chemo_Cell_Types_v2.h5ad"))

# 2. Pull the counts matrix (transposed automatically into [genes x cells])
counts_xenium <- t(adata$layers[["counts"]])

# 3. Extract the Xenium single-cell centroids matrix from obsm
# Typically saved as "spatial" or "X_spatial" in Scanpy/Squidpy
spatial_coords <- as.matrix(adata$obsm[["spatial"]])
colnames(spatial_coords) <- c("x", "y")
rownames(spatial_coords) <- adata$obs_names

# 4. Create the final SpatialExperiment container
spatial_spe <- SpatialExperiment(
    assays = list(counts = counts_xenium),
    colData = adata$obs,
    spatialCoords = spatial_coords
)
```

3. Run CellChat using Xenium labels 
```{r}
adata <- read_h5ad("./Graham_Chemo_Cell_Types_RCTD.h5ad")
adata <- adata[!is.na(adata$obs[["RCTD_corrected"]]), ]
# 2. Pull the counts matrix (transposed automatically into [genes x cells])
log_xenium <- t(adata$layers[["lognorm"]])

# 3. Extract the Xenium single-cell centroids matrix from obsm
# Typically saved as "spatial" or "X_spatial" in Scanpy/Squidpy
meta_data <- adata$obs
rownames(meta_data) <- adata$obs_names
# each tissue region is a sample: 5 samples, one condition (chemo), on 2 slides
#   chemo1: Chemo reg1, reg2, reg3   |   chemo2: Chemo reg4, reg6
meta_data$samples <- droplevels(factor(meta_data$region))
stopifnot(nlevels(meta_data$samples) == 5)
table(meta_data$samples, meta_data$samp)
spatial_coords <- as.matrix(meta_data[, c("x", "y")])
colnames(spatial_coords) <- c("x", "y")
rownames(spatial_coords) <- adata$obs_names
# SpatialCellChat's distance calculation ignores `samples`, and regions on different
# slides share one micron frame, so shift each sample along x (gap >> interaction
# range) to stop cells from different samples being treated as neighbors
sample_offset <- (as.integer(meta_data$samples) - 1) * (max(spatial_coords[, "x"]) + 5000)
spatial_coords[, "x"] <- spatial_coords[, "x"] + sample_offset
# Spatial factor of spatial coordinates
spot.size <- 10   # typical cell diameter (um) for single-cell resolution data
spatial.factors <- list(ratio = 1, tol = spot.size / 2)
```
```{r}
# cell groups = RCTD_corrected labels (drop any unused factor levels)
meta_data$RCTD_corrected <- droplevels(factor(meta_data$RCTD_corrected))
cellchat <- createSpatialCellChat(object = log_xenium, meta = meta_data,
                                  group.by = "RCTD_corrected", datatype = "spatial",
                                  coordinates = spatial_coords,
                                  spatial.factors = spatial.factors)
table(cellchat@idents)
```

```{r}
# ligand-receptor database: mouse, protein signaling only (subsetDB default drops non-protein)
cellchat@DB <- subsetDB(CellChatDB.mouse)

# keep signaling genes, then find over-expressed genes / L-R pairs per cell group
cellchat <- subsetData(cellchat)
cellchat <- identifyOverExpressedGenes(cellchat)
cellchat <- identifyOverExpressedInteractions(cellchat, variable.both = FALSE)
nrow(cellchat@LR$LRsig)   # L-R pairs measurable with the 300-gene panel
```
```{r}
# SpatialCellChat 0.1.0 builds dense cell x cell matrices (295 GB for distances,
# 314 GB for FN1_CD44 alone). These patches compute the same values only for
# neighboring cells (checked identical to the original on a 2,216-cell region).
source("./CellChat/spatialcellchat_sparse_patches.R")
future::plan("sequential")   # workers reload the unpatched package and copy ~1.5 GB each

# cell-level communication: diffusible signals up to 100 um, contact-dependent within 20 um
# scale.distance = 1: closest cell pair is 1.56 um, package requires min scaled distance in [1, 2]
cellchat <- computeCommunProb(cellchat, distance.use = TRUE,
                              interaction.range = 100, scale.distance = 1,
                              contact.dependent = TRUE, contact.range = 20)
cellchat <- filterCommunication(cellchat, min.cells = 10)
saveRDS(cellchat, "./CellChat/cellchat_filtered.rds")
# group-level communication + permutation p-values (creates net$prob / net$pval);
# without it, computeCommunProbPathway partial-matches net$prob to the 192k x 192k
# net$prob.cell and runs out of memory
cellchat <- computeAvgCommunProb(cellchat)
cellchat <- computeCommunProbPathway(cellchat)
cellchat <- aggregateNet(cellchat)
saveRDS(cellchat, "./CellChat/cellchat_RCTD_corrected.rds")
cellchat@netP$pathways
```

```{r}
# re-source patches: includes the fix for "should not be called with handlers on the stack"
source("./CellChat/spatialcellchat_sparse_patches.R")
cellchat <- netAnalysis_computeCentrality(
```

```{r}
cellchat <- readRDS("./CellChat/cellchat_RCTD_corrected.rds")
# cell types (RCTD_corrected) in space, one panel per sample
# (Xenium = one label per cell, so no `proportion`; that is for Visium deconvolution
#  pie charts. spatialDimPlot can't split samples, and the x offset squashes all 5 together)
df_sp <- data.frame(cellchat@images$coordinates, cell_type = cellchat@idents,
                    sample = cellchat@meta$samples)
cols_ct <- setNames(scPalette(nlevels(df_sp$cell_type)), levels(df_sp$cell_type))
plots_sp <- lapply(levels(df_sp$sample), function(s) {
  ggplot(df_sp[df_sp$sample == s, ], aes(x_cent, y_cent, color = cell_type)) +
    geom_point(size = 1, stroke = 0) +
    scale_color_manual(values = cols_ct, limits = names(cols_ct)) +
    scale_y_reverse() + coord_fixed() +
    guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3))) +
    theme_void() + labs(title = s, color = "RCTD_corrected") +
    if (s != levels(df_sp$sample)[1]) guides(color = "none")
})
wrap_plots(plots_sp, nrow = 2) + plot_layout(guides = "collect")
```

```{r}
library(ComplexHeatmap)
library(RColorBrewer)

# signalingRole_network reads cellchat@netP$centr (per cell type x pathway).
# The earlier centrality chunk used slot.name = "net" -> stored in net$centr, not netP,
# and readRDS() above reloads the object anyway. Compute pathway-level centrality here:
if (length(cellchat@netP$centr) == 0) {
  cellchat <- netAnalysis_computeCentrality(cellchat, slot.name = "netP", do.group = TRUE)
}
netAnalysis_signalingRole_network(
  cellchat, signaling = pathway.show, slot.name = "netP",
  measure = c("outdeg","indeg"), measure.name = c("Sender","Receiver"),
  width = 8, height = 3, font.size = 10
)
```

```{r, fig.width=20, fig.height=8}
pathway.show="CXCL"
# IL6 senders and receivers in space, per cell, one column per sample
# Sender = sum of a cell's outgoing IL6 probabilities (weighted out-degree),
# Receiver = sum of incoming (weighted in-degree); grey = 0. Color capped at the 99th percentile.
P_path <- cellchat@netP$tmp$prob.cell[[pathway.show]]      # cell x cell, rows send -> columns receive
df_role <- data.frame(cellchat@images$coordinates, cell_type = cellchat@idents,
                      sample = cellchat@meta$samples,
                      Sender = Matrix::rowSums(P_path), Receiver = Matrix::colSums(P_path))
plot_role <- function(role) {
  vmax <- quantile(df_role[[role]][df_role[[role]] > 0], 0.99)
  lapply(levels(df_role$sample), function(s) {
    d <- df_role[df_role$sample == s, ]
    d <- d[order(d[[role]]), ]                                  # strongest cells drawn on top
    ggplot(d, aes(x_cent, y_cent, color = pmin(.data[[role]], vmax))) +
      geom_point(data = d[d[[role]] == 0, ], color = "grey88", size = 0.1, stroke = 0) +
      geom_point(data = d[d[[role]] > 0, ], size = 0.25, stroke = 0) +
      scale_color_viridis_c(option = "magma", direction = -1, limits = c(0, vmax), name = role) +
      scale_y_reverse() + coord_fixed() + theme_void() +
      labs(title = paste(s, "-", role))
  })
}
wrap_plots(c(plot_role("Sender"), plot_role("Receiver")), nrow = 2) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") +
  plot_annotation(title = paste(pathway.show, "signaling: sending and receiving strength per cell"))

# which cell types are sending / receiving IL6 (number of cells with non-zero strength)
aggregate(cbind(sender_cells = Sender > 0, receiver_cells = Receiver > 0) ~ cell_type, df_role, sum)
```
```{r}
pathway.show <- "CSF"
ct.T     <- "T cells"
ct.mac   <- c("Arg1+ Macrophages", "Cxcl10+ Macrophages", "Cycling Macrophages",
              "Tissue Resident Macrophages", "DCs")
ct.tumor <- c("Epi Cancer", "Cycling Epi Cancer", "Mes Cancer", "Cycling Mes Cancer")
ct.focus <- c(ct.T, ct.mac, ct.tumor)

# relative contribution of each L-R pair to CXCL
netAnalysis_contribution(cellchat, signaling =pathway.show) 

# 1) every significant CXCL L-R pair among T cemor cells
netVisual_bubble(cellchat, signaling = pathway.show,
                 sources.use = ct.focus, targets.use=ct.focus, 
                 remove.isolate = TRUE, sort.by.target = TRUE, angle.x = 90,
                 title.name = "CXCL L-R pairs: tumor")
```
```{r, fig.width=12, fig.height=6}
# 2) what recruits T cells: all senders -> T cells (Cxcl9/10/13 -> Cxcr3, Cxcl16 -> Cxcr6, Cxcl12 -> Cxcr4)
netVisual_bubble(cellchat, signaling = pathway.show, 
                 targets.use = ct.T, remove.isolate = TRUE, angle.x = 90,
                 title.name = "CXCL signaling to T cells")
# 3) what macrophages/DCs and tumor cells send (to any receiver)
netVisual_bubble(cellchat, signaling = pathway.show, 
                 sources.use = c(ct.mac, ct.tumor), remove.isolate = TRUE, angle.x = 90,
                 title.name = "CXCL signaling from macrophages/DCs and tumor")
```
